stories.headline: A neutrino hunter at the South Pole wins the physics Nobel
stories.summary: The Belgian physicist Francis Halzen, of the University of Wisconsin–Madison, has been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for 2026. The citation names his decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin. He is the observatory's principal investigator; it stands at the Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station in Antarctica and has been operational since 2010.

stories.headline: Kosovo's Assembly elects Justina Shiroka-Pula as president
stories.summary: The Assembly of Kosovo elected Justina Shiroka-Pula as president on 6 October 2026, with 81 votes. She is an economist and academic who was Minister of Energy and Mining from 2008 to 2011 and the first woman to lead the Kosova Academy of Sciences and Arts. She has served as president since 7 October, the third woman to hold the office.

stories.headline: Laos has a new prime minister
stories.summary: The National Assembly of Laos has approved Saleumxay Kommasith as prime minister, a post he has held since 5 October 2026. He was a deputy prime minister from 2022 to 2026 and before that Minister of Foreign Affairs, from April 2016 to November 2024. He succeeds Sonexay Siphandone, who became National Assembly president.

stories.headline: Wasps move into the chambers Borneo trees build for ants
stories.summary: Scientists studying the tropical forests of Malaysian Borneo have found an unexpected shift in a long-running partnership. For at least 10 million years these ant-plants have produced hollow chambers where ants can live, and have supplied them with nutritious food bodies. Adult wasps are now using the same cavities, storing flies they have paralysed there as food for their young.
